samples.summary: Feature is inert on the pinned SDK, yet the Settings toggle ships anyway — the exact thing the design's Rollout section forbids
samples.evidence: `MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23"` and `supportsClientKey()` gates the whole durable path, but `packages/frontend/package.json:65` pins `"@yorkie-js/react": "0.7.22"` and this diff does not bump it (it only adds `fake-indexeddb`). `useDurableDocument` puts `supportsClientKey()` first in its `eligible` conjunction, so no document is ever durable in this build — the comment in `yorkie-capabilities.ts` says as much ("Bumping the dependency is the only action needed to turn the feature on"). Meanwhile `app/settings/page.tsx` ships the switch with copy stating "Keeps edits that have not reached the server on this device, so they survive a reload or a crash while you are offline... turning it off deletes what was stored." docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md § Rollout states the rule this breaks verbatim: "A control that ships before its behavior is not a dark launch; it is a control that does nothing. The preference may land early because nothing reads it; the toggle may not." A user who enables it gets the stated outcome ("edits survive a reload") not at all, and is told data was deleted that was never stored.

samples.summary: `durable` is not derived from the store actually working, so the chip can promise "Saved to this device" when IndexedDB is unavailable, quota is exhausted, or writes are failing
samples.evidence: The context value is `{ store, durable: !lost, reportLoss }`, and `lost` is set only by `DurableLossWatch` on the SDK's `local-changes-dropped` event. Nothing observes store write failures. docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md § What the user sees specifies `durable` as "the conjunction of three facts: this tab won the app lock, no `PersistDisabled` event has latched this document off, **and the store is not failing its writes**", and tabulates four rows that must set `durable=false` — IndexedDB unavailable (private browsing), document too large, quota exhausted after eviction, store writes failing — each with its own tooltip reason. None is reachable: `WafflebaseDocStore` rejects (quota, `InvalidStateError` after eviction, a failed `open()`) and the provider never learns. The cost is the one direction the design says the feature must not fail in — over-reporting durability — with the `beforeunload` guard simultaneously suppressed because `stranded` is false.

samples.summary: Neither of the design's chip-side affordances landed: the chip offers no way to enable offline saving, and `Not saved` never names which case applies
samples.evidence: docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md § Turning it on specifies "Two entry points, because the Settings page is not where someone is standing when they need this" — Settings *and* the sync chip — and its Rollout row for PR 4 lists "the Settings + chip opt-in". `grep setOfflinePersistenceEnabled` finds exactly one non-test caller, `app/settings/page.tsx:114`. The same doc's reason table ends "Because `Not saved` is now a *designed* state rather than the only state — the second tab, an oversized document, a broken store — ... Its tooltip must name which case applies"; `tooltipFor`'s `not-saved` arm still returns the single pre-existing string. The feature remains reachable through Settings, so the cost is discoverability and diagnosability rather than the stated outcome.

samples.summary: The design's explicit `YorkieProvider` memoization trap is not addressed — no React key covering docKey (and the preference) on the nested durable provider
samples.evidence: docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md flags it as a `> **Trap.**`: "`YorkieProvider` memoizes its client on `[apiKey, rpcAddr]` only. Navigating from document A to B changes `key` and `store` without recreating the client, so the provider must be given a React key covering both the document and the preference — ``key={`${docKey}:${enabled}`}`` — which also makes toggling the setting mid-session take effect." `CollabDocumentProvider` renders `<DurableYorkieProvider clientKey={clientKey} ...>` with no React `key`, so an in-place docKey change reconciles the same instance. If the memoization still holds in the target version, document B runs on document A's client key and store scope. (The preference half is covered incidentally, since toggling off changes the rendered tree shape.)

samples.summary: Recovery diverges from the reuse the design names (`DocumentCopyService` / `POST /documents/:id/copy`) and hand-rolls a note writer that duplicates `applyImportedContent`'s headless-client lifecycle
samples.evidence: docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md § Losing work anyway says "we already have the machinery for it in `DocumentCopyService` / `POST /documents/:id/copy`", and its See Also lists "document-copy.md — the copy engine the offline-copy recovery path reuses". The implementation instead calls `createDocument` + `applyImportedContent`, which is a defensible reuse choice (the copy endpoint copies a server-side document, not local bytes) — but the design was not updated to record it, so the doc now describes a reuse that did not happen. Separately, `writeNote()` re-creates the `new Client(...)` / `activate` / `attach` / `detach` / `deactivate` sequence that `app/documents/apply-imported-content.ts:190` already owns, rather than extending `ImportedContent` with a `note` arm; the two will now drift on any change to that lifecycle.

samples.summary: One row of the design's cleanup table — "workspace access lost" — has no trigger
samples.evidence: docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md § Storage tabulates cleanup triggers as: logout, "Document deleted, **or workspace access lost**", periodic 30-day, and quota eviction. `purgeOfflineDocuments` is wired only into `deleteDocument`/`deleteDocuments` in `api/documents.ts`; nothing purges when a user is removed from a workspace or loses access to a shared document, so that content stays on disk for up to thirty days after the authority to read it ends. The store already exposes `purgeDocument`, so this is a missing call site rather than missing machinery.

finding.summary: Feature is inert on the pinned SDK, yet the Settings toggle ships anyway — the exact thing the design's Rollout section forbids
finding.evidence: `MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23"` and `supportsClientKey()` gates the whole durable path, but `packages/frontend/package.json:65` pins `"@yorkie-js/react": "0.7.22"` and this diff does not bump it (it only adds `fake-indexeddb`). `useDurableDocument` puts `supportsClientKey()` first in its `eligible` conjunction, so no document is ever durable in this build — the comment in `yorkie-capabilities.ts` says as much ("Bumping the dependency is the only action needed to turn the feature on"). Meanwhile `app/settings/page.tsx` ships the switch with copy stating "Keeps edits that have not reached the server on this device, so they survive a reload or a crash while you are offline... turning it off deletes what was stored." docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md § Rollout states the rule this breaks verbatim: "A control that ships before its behavior is not a dark launch; it is a control that does nothing. The preference may land early because nothing reads it; the toggle may not." A user who enables it gets the stated outcome ("edits survive a reload") not at all, and is told data was deleted that was never stored.

verdict.reason: Every claimed element is present as described. `MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23"` (yorkie-capabilities.ts:24) is compared against the build constant injected straight from the dependency pin (vite.config.ts:360-364), and that pin is `"@yorkie-js/react": "0.7.22"` (package.json:65), so `atLeast` returns false and `supportsClientKey()` is false in this build. That call is the first term of the `eligible` conjunction in `useDurableDocument` (use-durable-document.ts:115-120), so no document can ever be durable. The repo's own task doc confirms it verbatim: "nothing writes to IndexedDB on this branch" and "Manual smoke — needs the dependency bump, since nothing durable mounts until the gate opens" (20260917-offline-wiring-todo.md:220, 242-246). Meanwhile the Settings page ships the switch unconditionally with copy promising edits "survive a reload or a crash" and that "turning it off deletes what was stored" (app/settings/page.tsx:98-116). The design's Rollout section forbids exactly this in so many words: "A control that ships before its behavior is not a dark launch; it is a control that does nothing. The preference may land early because nothing reads it; the toggle may not" (docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:394-401). No guard elsewhere hides the toggle, and this is a spec-conformance mismatch with user-facing cost (stated outcome unavailable, false claim of deletion), so it is in-lane and blocking.

Nothing observes store write failures. docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md § What the user sees specifies `durable` as "the conjunction of three facts: this tab won the app lock, no `PersistDisabled` event has latched this document off, **and the store is not failing its writes**", and tabulates four rows that must set `durable=false` — IndexedDB unavailable (private browsing), document too large, quota exhausted after eviction, store writes failing — each with its own tooltip reason. None is reachable: `WafflebaseDocStore` rejects (quota, `InvalidStateError` after eviction, a failed `open()`) and the provider never learns. verdict.reason: No counterexample exists in the tree. `durable` is produced at durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:104-109 as `!lost`, and `lost` has a single writer — `reportLoss`, called only from `DurableLossWatch`'s `local-changes-dropped` subscription (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:160-163). A repo-wide grep for `reportLoss|setLost|durable:` surfaces no other producer, and `PersistDisabled` has no handler anywhere (only a comment in sync-state.ts:44 and the design doc). `WafflebaseDocStoreOptions` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:104-138) exposes no failure/health callback; the store communicates failure only by rejecting (refuseIfEvicted throws at :617-626, quota rethrow at :1007-1012) and nothing in the app awaits or observes those rejections — `OfflineRuntime` swallows its own into console.warn, and the SDK-facing calls have no app-side catch. The durable branch in collab-document-provider.tsx:203-226 / use-durable-document.ts:115-120 gates only on lock election, preference, capability and key prefix; there is no IndexedDB availability probe (offline-persistence-preference.ts:40-57 explicitly declines to infer it, matching the doc's instruction at offline-local-persistence.md:130-138). Consequence is user-facing and blocking under the spec-conformance lens: the doc's Goal (:52-53) and § What the user sees table (:326-338, four rows that must set durable=false with distinct tooltips) are unmet, so the chip can show "Saved to this device" (sync-status-chip.tsx:41, sync-state.ts:85) while nothing is on disk, and because `stranded` is false in that state the beforeunload/navigation guard (sync-status-chip.tsx:106-158) is simultaneously suppressed — over-reporting durability, the one direction the design says must not fail.

finding.summary: The chip opt-in entry point specified by the design (and listed in PR 4's contents) is not implemented — Settings is the only way to enable offline saving
finding.evidence: offline-local-persistence.md § Turning it on: "Two entry points, because the Settings page is not where someone is standing when they need this: **Settings** — a switch... **The sync chip** — which already reports durability, so it is the natural place to offer acquiring it"; the durability table's first row is "Offer to turn it on — this is the one row that is a call to action rather than a fault"; and the rollout table gives PR 4 as "the Settings + chip opt-in". The chip only maps states to labels/tooltips (LABELS/ICONS/tooltipFor) and never reads or writes `offline-persistence-preference`; `useOfflinePersistenceEnabled` is imported only by `app/settings/page.tsx` and `use-durable-document.ts`. A user stranded on `Not saved` has no way to acquire durability where they feel the need, which is the stated reason the second entry point exists.

verdict.reason: The design specifies two opt-in entry points (offline-local-persistence.md:140-147), makes the chip's "Offer to turn it on" its own durability-table row (:333), assigns "the Settings + chip opt-in" to PR 4 (:387), and rests a risk mitigation on it (:417). I read sync-status-chip.tsx in full: it only maps states to LABELS/ICONS/tooltipFor plus toast and unload/navigation guards, with no enable affordance and no tooltip branch for "offline saving not enabled". Searching wider than the reviewer did, a repo-wide grep for setOfflinePersistenceEnabled shows the only non-test production caller is the Settings switch (app/settings/page.tsx:114); a case-insensitive "offline" sweep of packages/frontend/src surfaces only offline-runtime.tsx (erase/collect/recovery toast — no enable offer) and the Settings section as UI. Candidate-copy greps ("Turn on", "Enable offline", "Offline saving", "this device") find enable wording only in settings/page.tsx:103-114. The repo's own task record corroborates: 20260917-offline-wiring-todo.md Task 3 covers only the saved-locally state (3.4 unchecked) and Task 8.1 lists only the Settings opt-in, with no deferral note for the chip. The version gate does not excuse it, since the Settings half shipped under the same gate. A user stranded on "Not saved" therefore cannot acquire durability where the design says they need it — an acceptance item from the design's PR-4 contents left unmet, which is a user-facing cost rather than tidiness.
